description: Transport- and backend-neutral Assignment Runtime API for one fenced authority realm and peer GUI, CLI, Agent, and KFX clients.

authority.realmRule: Exactly one declared Assignment transition authority is active for a realm generation.
authority.clientRule: Clients submit commands and consume receipts; they never mutate backend storage directly.
authority.rootParity: Equivalent clients observing the same realm revision receive identical canonical identities, state roots, Fact/Episode references, and receipt roots.

transports.semantics: in-process adapter with the same request, response, fencing, and receipt contract
same-host authenticated transport with reconnect and event-resume semantics
may implement the same protocol later; no database, scheduler, HA, or capacity behavior is implied

concurrency.revision: Every successful read names the observed realm revision and root.
concurrency.cas: Every state-changing command carries expectedRevision and fails with stale-revision before mutation when it differs.
concurrency.generation: Every request and response names the realm generation; an older generation fails with generation-fenced.
concurrency.claimAndLease: Claim and phase commands bind the exact attempt, active lease or Warrant, Assignment identity, and expected revision.
concurrency.singleWriter: No adapter may fall through to direct storage or a second writer when the realm runtime is unavailable.

idempotency.sameKeySameBody: Return the original command and receipt roots with disposition=replayed and perform no second mutation.
idempotency.sameKeyDifferentBody: Fail with idempotency-conflict and perform no mutation.
idempotency.unknownOutcome: An operator may abandon only the local pending projection under exact command, plan, revision, actor, reason, and evidence roots; the authority outcome remains unknown and the original command identity can never be replayed.
idempotency.retention: The realm advertises the bounded replay window through capability discovery.

workSemantics.publicFields: Stable logical identities, enums, revisions, receipts, and SHA-256 content roots only; adopter payloads and transport details remain private.
workSemantics.freshness: A successor input snapshot invalidates every run and effect authorization bound to an earlier snapshot.
workSemantics.attemptFence: Every write binds the exact Assignment, Attempt, active lease, realm generation, and expected revision before authority mutation.
workSemantics.effectSettlement: Authorization, attempt-before-transport, transport outcome, business outcome, and accepted completion are distinct records.
workSemantics.ambiguousOutcome: A missing or unknown transport outcome, or transport acceptance without a known business outcome, requires reconciliation and never permits blind repeat.
workSemantics.completion: When Work semantics records exist, completion requires settled accepted effects and proof roots for the current input snapshot, managed run, and effect outcomes.

events.resume: Resume after the exact acknowledged cursor without duplicating an applied command.
events.gap: If the cursor is outside retained history, fail with event-resume-gap and return a recovery snapshot revision; never guess a successor cursor.
events.reconnect: Reconnect re-negotiates capabilities and generation before resuming.

localRuntimeProfile.crashRule: A command is successful only when its authoritative receipt is durable; process liveness is diagnostic, not proof.
localRuntimeProfile.reconnectRule: Clients rediscover capability and generation, then resume from an exact cursor or recovery snapshot.
localRuntimeProfile.migrationSeam: Backend replacement preserves protocol identities, revisions, roots, receipts, error codes, CAS, idempotency, and event-resume behavior.

nonClaims: The contract document alone does not certify an installed Runtime build or adopter integration.
This contract does not migrate, initialize, or mutate a real Home Workspace.
This contract does not qualify PostgreSQL, distributed scheduling, multi-host recovery, high availability, sharding, or capacity.
Registering the contract does not prove that existing GUI, CLI, Agent, or KFX paths already consume it.
